2019-0.label: Cached and Confused: Web Cache Deception in the Wild

details.title: Cached and Confused: Web Cache Deception in the Wild
details.summary: Web cache deception exploits path confusion: a URL such as /account.php/nonexistent.jpg looks static to a caching proxy but resolves to a private page at the origin, so the cache stores it for any attacker to fetch. A measurement of 340 top sites found leaked personal data, session and CSRF tokens, plus five path-confusion variants that widen the attack.

details.title: [🌐💧💥] HTTP Cache Cross-Site Leaks
details.summary: The browser HTTP cache answers cross-site questions: evict a resource with a POST or an overlong Referer, make the victim load a target page, then re-probe to see whether it got cached. That reveals whether the page requested a given resource, leaking group membership, search hits and other private state; partitioned caches and SameSite cookies mitigate it.

2019-5.label: All is XSS that comes to the .NET

details.title: All is XSS that comes to the .NET
details.summary: ASP.NET still accepts a cookieless session segment such as (A(...)) anywhere in a URL path, and Control.ResolveUrl copies that attacker-controlled segment into every app-root-relative URL it emits. Injecting a quote and an event handler there escapes the src or href attribute for XSS, with ES6 template literals supplying payloads that need no parentheses, plus or slash.

details.title: Filling in the Blanks: Exploiting Null Byte Buffer Overflow for a $40,000 Bounty

Repeating a POST full of %00 bytes returned megabytes of adjacent server memory, including RSA private keys, other users' page DOMs, plaintext credentials and internal HTTP requests.

2019-11.label: Facebook Messenger server random memory exposure through corrupted GIF

details.title: Facebook Messenger server random memory exposure through corrupted GIF image
details.summary: Uploading a GIF whose header declares a canvas size but carries no image data made the Facebook Messenger server-side renderer return a picture filled with uninitialised memory. Repeated uploads of the same file returned different pictures, leaking fragments of server memory left by other activity; the bug paid 10,000 dollars.

2019-12.label: Let's Make Windows Defender Angry: Antivirus can be an oracle!

details.title: Let's Make Windows Defender Angry: Antivirus can be an oracle!
details.summary: AVOracle turns antivirus into a side channel: when a file holds both attacker-controlled data and a secret, a JScript or HTML payload split around the secret makes Windows Defender flag the file only for the right guess, leaking the secret byte by byte. Because Defender also blanks the matched bytes, the same trick deletes log entries and corrupts structured files.

details.title: [CB19] Let's Make Windows Defender Angry: Antivirus can be an oracle! by Ryo Ichikawa
At Home Among Strangers
details.summary: Reverse proxies append the real client IP to X-Forwarded-For, so a spoofed value is normally harmless. Placing a bare carriage return in the header makes some back ends stop parsing at the CR and trust the attacker's value instead, defeating IP allowlists that guard admin interfaces.

2019-14.label: Exploiting padding oracles with fixed IVs

details.title: Exploiting padding oracles with fixed IVs
details.summary: A session token is encrypted with AES-CBC but never signed and uses a fixed IV, so a padding oracle can forge chosen plaintext apart from one uncontrollable random block. Reusing the leading blocks of a freely issued anonymous token moves that junk inside a JSON string, and a second user property placed after it wins in JSON.parse, producing an admin token.

details.title: XSS in GMail's AMP4Email via DOM Clobbering
details.summary: AMP4Email in Gmail allowed the id attribute, so DOM clobbering was possible. Two anchors sharing an id yield an HTMLCollection whose members can be addressed by name, and an anchor stringifies to its href, letting an attacker clobber the AMP_MODE and testLocation globals and point AMP's script loader at an attacker URL for XSS.

details.title: Abusing HTTP hop-by-hop request headers
details.summary: Naming arbitrary headers in the HTTP Connection header marks them hop-by-hop, and proxies that forward that list instead of consuming it let an attacker delete headers a downstream hop added. Removing X-Forwarded-For can make an application treat the request as internal, and the trick also fingerprints caches, bypasses WAF rules that require a header, and can poison caches with error responses.

2019-27.label: Don't open that XML: XXE to RCE in XML plugins for VS Code, Eclipse, Theia, ...

details.title: Shielder - Don’t open that XML: XXE to RCE in XML plugins for VS Code, Eclipse, Theia, …
details.summary: The LSP4XML language server parses XML as soon as an editor opens or saves it, so a malicious file triggers an external entity fetch with no further user action. 2019-31.label: IIS Application vs. Folder Detection During Blackbox Testing

details.title: IIS Application vs. Folder Detection During Blackbox Testing
details.summary: Requesting a built-in ASP.NET service endpoint such as profile_json_appservice.axd/jsdebug under any path reveals whether that path is an IIS application, which answers with 200 and JavaScript, or merely a folder, which answers 500. Knowing which decides whether an upload can become code execution via web.config and supplies the application path needed to forge ViewState payloads.

details.summary: ASP.NET signs and encrypts the __VIEWSTATE parameter using machineKey values, so when MAC validation is disabled or the validation and decryption keys leak, an attacker forges a ViewState carrying a serialisation gadget and executes code on the server. Covers a ysoserial.net plugin, legacy .NET behaviour, recovering the application path, __EVENTVALIDATION, and WAF evasion.

2019-33.label: The Cookie Monster in Your Browsers

details.title: The Cookie Monster in Your Browsers
details.summary: A tour of how browsers and servers disagree about cookies: a subdomain can force a cookie onto its parent (cookie tossing), oversized cookies make a server reject requests (cookie bomb), and servers that still split on commas accept injected cookies. The result is CSRF token fixation, an HttpOnly bypass, and stealing OAuth authorization codes via a bombed redirect.

2019-35.label: XSS-Auditor --- the protector of unprotected and the deceiver of protected

details.title: XSS-Auditor — the protector of unprotected
details.summary: Chrome's XSS Auditor was reverted from block mode to filter mode, so instead of stopping a page it silently strips the matched script. Reflecting a fake match aimed at a page's own defensive script deletes that script, and a CTF write-up shows this turning an otherwise blocked injection into working XSS.

details.summary: Firefox for iOS executed javascript URIs supplied by its built-in QR code scanner, so scanning a crafted code ran script in the context of the page the user was already viewing and could read its contents and cookies. It also worked in reader mode, on local files and internal pages, and ignored the site's content security policy. Opera Mini for iOS was affected too.

details.title: Backchannel Leaks on Strict Content-Security Policy
details.summary: Under a strict default-src 'self' policy the browser still allows outbound requests to unapproved hosts. 2019-47.label: Bypassing SOP Using the Browser Cache

details.title: Bypassing SOP using the browser cache
details.summary: The browser cache is keyed only on the absolute URL, with no record of which origin requested it. A JSONP or CORS response cached after a legitimate same-site request is handed back to any site that requests the same URL, so Referer, Origin, SameSite and custom-header checks never run because the request never reaches the server.

details.title: Alexey Tiurin - Reverse proxies & Inconsistency
Reverse proxies & Inconsistency
details.summary: Reverse proxies, caches and load balancers decode and normalise URLs differently from the origin server, so path parameters, encoded dot-segments and double slashes make the two disagree about which path a request is for. The mismatch bypasses proxy access rules, misroutes requests, strips or adds security headers, and enables web cache deception and cache poisoning.

2019-49.label: x-up-devcap-post-charset Header in ASP.NET to Bypass WAFs Again

details.title: x-up-devcap-post-charset Header in ASP.NET to Bypass WAFs Again!
details.summary: When the User-Agent starts with UP, ASP.NET takes the request body charset from the non-standard x-up-devcap-post-charset header instead of the Content-Type charset directive. An attacker encodes a POST payload in an exotic codepage such as ibm500, so a WAF that only whitelists Content-Type charsets sees nothing while the application decodes the attack.

details.title: Iframes/Popups Are Dangerous in Mobile WebView: Studying and Mitigating Differential Context Vulnerabilities
details.summary: Android WebView lets an untrusted iframe or popup share context with the host page, a class the authors call differential context vulnerabilities. An embedded frame can forge web messaging, reach app-exposed mobile functionality and mount phishing; an automated scanner found the flaw widespread, including in Facebook, Skype and Uber.

2019-53.label: Leaky Images: Targeted Privacy Attacks in the Web

details.title: Leaky Images: Targeted Privacy Attacks in the Web
details.summary: An image shared privately with one user is requested by an attacker-controlled page, and the load succeeds only for that logged-in user, revealing that a specific person is visiting the site. It needs neither JavaScript nor CSS, extends to tracking groups and linking identities across sites, and affected eight of the thirty most popular image-sharing sites including Facebook and Twitter.

details.title: USENIX Security '19 - Leaky Images: Targeted Privacy Attacks in the Web
Bypassing CSP with policy injection
details.summary: A URL parameter reflected into a CSP report-uri directive lets an attacker append directives to the policy. On Edge a semicolon and underscore make the syntax invalid so the whole policy is dropped, and on Chrome an appended script-src-elem directive overrides the existing script-src, in both cases restoring script execution and turning a blocked injection into working XSS.

2019-55.label: JavaScript Template Attacks: Automatically Inferring Host Information for Targeted Exploits

details.title: JavaScript Template Attacks: Automatically Inferring Host Information for Targeted Exploits
details.summary: An automated method records every property JavaScript can read in many environments and builds templates from them, so a property stable on one system but different on another leaks the host. Two new side channels also reveal the CPU instruction set and the memory allocator, defeating anti-fingerprinting in Firefox, Chrome, Edge and mobile Tor and guiding targeted exploits.

details.title: NDSS 2019 JavaScript Template Attacks: Automatically Inferring Host Info for Targeted Exploits

2019-56.label: What Are You Searching For? A Remote Keylogging Attack on Search Engine Autocomplete

details.title: What Are You Searching For? A Remote Keylogging Attack on Search Engine Autocomplete
details.summary: Search autocomplete fires a request per keystroke, so an eavesdropper on encrypted traffic can combine packet inter-arrival timing, the percent-encoded Space character in the query URL, and HTTP/2 HPACK static Huffman code lengths to reconstruct what was typed. Up to 15 percent of queries were identified from a 12,000-word dictionary.

details.title: USENIX Security '19 - What Are You Searching For? A Remote Keylogging Attack
Cross-Site Challenge-Response Attacks
details.summary: Brute-forces password and secret-code challenge-response checks across origins by making visitors' browsers submit guesses and reading success from side channels that survive the same-origin policy. One variant turns any page visitor into a guessing bot, another targets the visitor's own account; a survey finds the weakness in popular sites, CMSs, routers and IoT devices.

2019-58.label: PhishFarm: A Scalable Framework for Measuring the Effectiveness of Evasion Techniques against Browser Phishing Blacklists

details.title: PhishFarm: A Scalable Framework for Measuring the Effectiveness of Evasion Techniques against Browser Phishing Blacklists
details.summary: PhishFarm deploys 2,380 live PayPal-branded decoy phishing sites on fresh .com domains, each behind one of six request filters taken from real phishing kits, reports them to 10 anti-phishing entities and times browser blacklisting. Cloaking by geolocation, device type or JavaScript cut the chance of blacklisting by over 55 percent, and mobile browsers failed to warn at all.

2019-59.label: All Your Clicks Belong to Me: Investigating Click Interception on the Web

details.title: All Your Clicks Belong to Me: Investigating Click Interception on the Web
details.summary: A measurement study of how third-party scripts steal user clicks. An instrumented browser framework called Observer analysed the Alexa top 250K sites and identified three interception techniques, finding 437 scripts that intercepted clicks on 613 sites. Most diverted clicks into advertising revenue and some delivered scamware.

details.title: USENIX Security '19 - All Your Clicks Belong to Me: Investigating Click Interception on the Web

2019-60.label: Latex Gloves: Protecting Browser Extensions from Probing and Revelation Attacks

details.title: Latex Gloves: Protecting Browser Extensions from Probing and Revelation Attacks
details.summary: Browser extensions give themselves away: a page can probe web-accessible resources by URL, and an extension that injects a WAR reference into the page reveals Firefox per-profile random UUID. Combining revelation with probing uniquely identifies about 90 percent of content-injecting extensions and yields a stable per-browser tracking identifier.

details.title: NDSS 2019 Latex Gloves: Protecting Browser Extensions from Probing and Revelation Attacks

2019-61.label: Scalable Scanning and Automatic Classification of TLS Padding Oracle Vulnerabilities

details.title: Scalable Scanning and Automatic Classification of TLS Padding Oracle Vulnerabilities
details.summary: First large-scale scan for CBC padding oracle flaws in TLS, using a reduced probe set and automatic classification of server response fingerprints. It found 1.83 percent of the Alexa Top Million vulnerable across nearly 100 distinct behaviours, many exploitable simply by observing differing responses rather than by precise timing measurement.

details.title: USENIX Security '19 - Scalable Scanning and Automatic Classification of TLS Padding Oracle

2019-62.label: Postcards from the Post-HTTP World: Amplification of HTTPS Vulnerabilities in the Web Ecosystem

details.title: Postcards from the Post-HTTP World: Amplification of HTTPS Vulnerabilities in the Web Ecosystem
details.summary: A crawl of the Alexa top 10k plus 90,816 dependency and sub-domain hosts maps still-exploitable TLS flaws such as ROBOT, DROWN, POODLE-TLS and Heartbleed onto attack trees, then measures the web-application damage. 898 sites become fully compromisable, 412 can have every session cookie stolen and 543 accept forced cookies, usually via a vulnerable related domain or script host.

details.title: Postcards from the Post HTTP World: Amplification of HTTPS Vulnerabilities in the Web Ecosystem
details.channel: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy

2019-63.label: The Betrayal at Cloud City: An Empirical Analysis of Cloud-Based Mobile Backends

details.title: The Betrayal At Cloud City: An Empirical Analysis Of Cloud-Based Mobile Backends
details.summary: An automated pipeline called SkyWalker extracts the backend URLs an Android app contacts and remotely vets those cloud services. Across the top 5,000 free Play Store apps it found 983 N-day and 655 0-day vulnerabilities in backend operating systems, services and web apps, exposing users of apps with 1M to 500M installs, often through third-party SDKs the developer never chose.

details.title: USENIX Security '19 - The Betrayal At Cloud City: An Empirical Analysis Of Cloud-Based Mobile

2019-64.label: Provoking browser quirks with behavioural fuzzing

details.title: Provoking browser quirks with behavioural fuzzing
details.summary: Behavioural fuzzing drives every Unicode code point into a chosen HTML or JavaScript position and diffs the parse result to expose browser quirks. In Firefox it shows a newline closing an HTML comment after an incomplete terminator, a null byte opening one, and certain code points being ignored by the JavaScript parser, each yielding a new filter-bypass XSS vector.

2019-65.label: Measuring and Analyzing Search Engine Poisoning of Linguistic Collisions

details.title: Measuring and Analyzing Search Engine Poisoning of Linguistic Collisions
details.summary: Misspellings that happen to be real words, often in another language, slip past search engines' auto-correction, so attackers can rank malicious pages against those queries. A crawl of 1.77 million misspelled searches on Google and Baidu, with a neural model to pick candidates, finds about 1.19 percent return malicious first-page results, concentrated in gambling, drugs and adult terms.

details.title: Measuring and Analyzing Search Engine Poisoning of Linguistic Collisions
details.channel: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy

details.title: Telerik Revisited
details.summary: Re-examines CVE-2017-11317 in Telerik UI for ASP.NET and finds it is more than an arbitrary file upload: the rauPostData blob carries an assembly-qualified type name handed to JavaScriptSerializer, giving arbitrary deserialization. Using AssemblyInstaller to load a mixed-mode DLL runs its DllMain, so unauthenticated code execution needs no write access to the web root.

details.context: Earlier research cited as a basis for this technique.

details.title: Re-Animating ActivitySurrogateSelector
details.summary: Microsoft's .NET 4.8 fix for the ActivitySurrogateSelector deserialization gadget is only a type check that a hidden app setting can disable. A still-working gadget, TextFormattingRunProperties driving XamlReader and ObjectDataProvider, sets that flag or writes the internal boolean by reflection, re-enabling arbitrary assembly loading and code execution from a deserialization sink.

details.title: ActivitySurrogateSelector bypass implementation
details.context: A companion code artifact linked by the original source.

2019-68.label: Practical Decryption exFiltration: Breaking PDF Encryption

details.title: Practical Decryption exFiltration: Breaking PDF Encryption
details.summary: Modified encrypted PDFs exfiltrate plaintext when their recipients decrypt them. Partial encryption permits attacker-controlled forms, links or scripts to reference encrypted objects; unauthenticated CBC and known permission bytes also enable encrypted gadgets. Tests on 27 viewers distinguish interaction requirements and full, partial or single-word leakage.

2019-69.label: The inception bar: a new phishing method

details.title: The inception bar: a new phishing method
details.summary: Demonstrates a fake address bar after mobile Chrome hides its toolbar during scrolling. A nested scrolling region and top-boundary reset keep the real toolbar hidden as the user scrolls upward. The technique needs an initial user scroll and matching browser behavior; it does not change the actual origin or require fullscreen permission.
